title: Design a versioned Next.js regression and release matrix
businessContext: A unit suite of policy models is labeled proof that every routing, cache and deployment behavior works on both major versions.
problemStatement: Design the system for Supported Next.js 15 maintenance and 16 stable; 100 practice scenarios. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Keep exact policy tests cheap and deterministic.
Verify representative real framework boundaries on both versions.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: Supported Next.js 15 maintenance and 16 stable; 100 practice scenarios
functional: Keep exact policy tests cheap and deterministic.
Verify representative real framework boundaries on both versions.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Use unit tests for pure input policies and curriculum integrity, production-server tests for routing/metadata/headers/actions/streaming, and deployment integration for CDN/cache handlers/queues/databases.

An always-green mock can conceal an unsupported API or a server cache leak. Introduce deliberate negative fixtures, assert real HTTP/output evidence and fail unsupported claims rather than manufacturing a passing score for guided work.
alternativeApproaches: Use a reviewed pinned release matrix and a separate dependency-update job. Unbounded latest installs can change the baseline silently; record exactly what was tested and refresh the version snapshot deliberately.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Run the supported-version fixtures from clean installs and production builds.
Mutate a policy/reference to prove the intended check fails.
Audit report wording against actual executed checks and retained evidence.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
